newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Tuesday unaffected by the Bank of Israel decision to lower its key interest rate, dealers said.
After the setting of the representative rate on Monday the Bank of Israel said it was lowering its key lending rate for January by 0.5 percentage point to an annualised 14.7 percent.

"Investors were expecting a moderate rate cut and it had no impact on local trading," said one dealer. "Trading was mixed and the shekel rose mildly because of strong activity on the part of options speculators."
He attributed the surge in options activity to the expiry of December Maof dollar options today.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2660 shekels against 3.2690 shekels on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6472 shekels against 3.6522 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8566 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8645 on Monday and against the mark at 2.1016 shekels against 2.1054 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2670 shekels.
